nodes.title: PREP 24 FPS VIDEO + PAIRED AUDIO (124 FRAMES)

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the same female easycore/pop-punk performer defined jointly by @hero_face for facial identity and @hero_look for full-body appearance, wardrobe, body proportions, and distinctive features. Preserve the exact reference styling: shaggy bright yellow hair with vivid pink streaks, dark eyeliner, a small silver septum ring, a black spiked choker with a silver center ring, a cropped black graphic T-shirt, black ripped skinny jeans, a silver hip chain, and worn black high-top sneakers.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The opening of a single uninterrupted easycore music-video take follows <Subject 1> from a backstage room toward a door as the first vocal begins, using @song for the performed song and musical backing.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve her facial identity, hairstyle, body proportions, wardrobe, colors, accessories, and distinctive features from @hero_face and @hero_look while allowing natural performance poses and expressions.
@song: reference - its English lyric content, female vocal delivery, melody, phrasing, rhythm, beat, and easycore/pop-punk instrumentation guide the generated performance without directly copying the source signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a photorealistic high-energy easycore/pop-punk music video presented as one uninterrupted moving-camera take. There are no cuts; camera movement, performer momentum, lighting, and physical space flow continuously into the next generated segment.
[Shot 1] A medium-wide front tracking shot begins in a dim backstage dressing room while <Subject 1> walks toward camera with relaxed confidence, the camera gliding backward at her pace. During the opening instrumental her mouth remains naturally closed; she rolls one shoulder and lightly catches the hem of her cropped black T-shirt, steps around a road case, and keeps moving toward a brightly lit door at the far end of the room. Practical fluorescent fixtures and a warm mirror-light strip slide past behind her, catching the vivid yellow hair, pink streaks, silver choker hardware, septum ring, and hip chain while creating strong parallax without any cut.

As the first vocal enters, <Subject 1> (S1) looks directly into the lens and sings with the energetic, clean female delivery referenced from @song, <d>[English] Left the room with the lights still on.</d> On “left the room,” she reaches the doorway while still walking; the camera eases into a three-quarter side angle and lets the lit dressing room remain visible behind her for one final moment. She pushes the door open with her shoulder and crosses the threshold without slowing.

Near the end of the segment the next phrase begins while she enters a narrow concrete service corridor: <Subject 1> (S1) continues, <d>[English] Hit the door and the hallway's gone.</d> The phrase remains in progress as the camera arcs around her right side. Beyond her, the corridor geometry begins to stretch unnaturally toward another opening, preparing the physical transformation that continues in the next segment. Keep her walking motion, the camera arc, and the door movement visibly in progress at the boundary.

overall_soundscape:
Low backstage room tone, soft shoe impacts, T-shirt fabric and hip-chain movement, and a door latch are audible beneath the performance.

non_diegetic_music:
@song is referenced for the fast easycore/pop-punk backing heard by the audience, including distorted guitars, bass, punchy live drums, melodic hooks, and the dynamic changes present in this song segment.
nodes.title: SCHEDULED REF2VA — COMPILES @TAGS PER SCENE

widgets_values:
1. Open the Scene Prompt Editor and select a scene. It edits the connected Plan directly.

2. Click @ Reference. The tray shows only references active for that scene and their current native labels. Hover an image/video tag to preview it. Hover audio for controls; it never autoplays. Click a chip to insert its stable @tag.

3. Queue from scene 1, or set Loop Start's range/resume controls. The Scheduled Ref2VA node compiles stable tags to native H3 labels and inserts no prompt text.

4. Review Gate pauses after each saved scene. Approve to continue, edit+retry to replace only that scene prompt, reroll for a new seed, or approve+stop to keep a recoverable partial.

5. Final Assemble uses %date:yyyy-MM-dd%. Existing exports are never overwritten: later runs receive _001, _002, and so on. The amber recovery branch remains muted until you need assembly without rerendering.
